repair_summary: Tighten _cli_start to wait for daemon_state to flip to online/degraded (instead of returning started=true on PID-file presence). Rewrite test_cli_start_returns_live_pid_after_worker_up to mock time.sleep against a fake_poll_tick that mirrors real worker disk writes.

done_definition: _cli_start reads daemon.status JSON directly via read_json_or_none(status_path()) — does NOT route through read_status_snapshot (which forces daemon_state=stopped on PID-death and would cause _cli_start to bail out after one poll during a graceful restart)
Polling loop exits only when daemon_state in (online, degraded); degraded path extracts the first required-service blocker into degraded_reason
Fast-fail path: when the spawned worker's PID is dead AND state is stopped/offline, the loop breaks immediately instead of waiting out start_timeout_s
Failure branch returns started=false, reason=start_failed, last_state, pid_alive and exit code 1 (instead of silently returning started=true with a green return code)
test_cli_start_returns_live_pid_after_worker_up passes; the rest of TestDaemonStopFlagLifecycle remains green
daemon.py (production) and test_daemon.py are the only files touched; WP02/WP03 files unchanged

code_evidence.test_daemon.py_lines_606_616: fake_sleep = side_effect that calls fake_poll_tick; mock.patch on daemon_module.time.sleep replaces time.sleep inside the polling loop
